_README: WHO AND WHAT MUST NEVER BE AUTO-TRASHED. Copy this file to protected.local.json and
fill it in for yourself - the .local.json is gitignored and never leaves your machine.
This is the guard behind the 'Always trash this sender' button and any future rule the
dashboard can write. It used to be a regex hard-coded in server.py, which meant one
person's relatives were compiled into the program - wrong for them if it ever shipped,
and wrong in principle: WHO MATTERS TO YOU is configuration, not code.
IT FAILS CLOSED. If protected.local.json is missing or unreadable, the dashboard
refuses to write ANY auto-trash rule at all. An absent guard must never read as
'nothing is protected' - that is the failure direction that silences family mail.
protected_names: _Names, surnames or sender strings that must never be locked to auto-trash._
_Matched case-insensitively as substrings, so a first name covers its variants._
_Put your family here, anyone whose mail you must never miss, your employer,_
_your banks, your doctor, your government correspondents._
_REPLACE THE LINES BELOW. They are underscore-prefixed on purpose: the dashboard_
_ignores any entry starting with _, so this file copied verbatim yields ZERO names_
_and the guard reports itself UNCONFIGURED rather than armed-but-protecting-nobody._
_Strip the leading underscore from each line you fill in._
_workflow_senders: Senders whose mail carries something you must DO, with a link, on a deadline.
They get their own panel above everything else and can push your phone.
The key is the exact From address; the value is [short-kind, human label].
The example below is a clinic; a school portal, a payroll system or a benefits
office works the same way. Replace it with whatever applies to you, or leave it
empty - an empty list simply means the panel never appears.
_workflow_link_domain: Links in workflow mail are only made CLICKABLE when the sender is verified (DKIM
passes for this domain) AND the link's own host is under it. Both must hold.
Leave empty to never linkify anything.
_rule_min_messages: How many messages before a sender may be locked to auto-trash.
